'''Callum Michael Roberts''' is a British [[marine conservation]] [[Marine biology|biologist]], [[oceanographer]], [[Science communication|science communicator]], author and research scholar at the [[University of Exeter]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Profile {{!}} Biosciences {{!}} University of Exeter|url=https://biosciences.exeter.ac.uk/staff/profile/index.php?web_id=Callum_Roberts|access-date=1 April 2021|website=biosciences.exeter.ac.uk}}</ref> He was formerly at the [[University of York]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Callum Roberts|url=http://www.york.ac.uk/environment/our-staff/callum-roberts/|publisher=The University of York|access-date=8 October 2010}}</ref> He is best known for his research and advocacy related to [[marine reserve]]s and the [[environmental impact of fishing]].

==Career==
Roberts' work examines the [[Human impact on marine life|impact of human activity]] on [[marine ecosystem]]s, particularly [[coral reef]]s. His research output has examined the benefits of [[marine reserve]]s and no-fishing zones on [[Sustainable fishery|sustainable fisheries]] and biodiversity.<ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Gell FR, Roberts CM |date=1 September 2003|title=Benefits beyond boundaries: the fishery effects of marine reserves |journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution|language=en|volume=18|issue=9|pages=448–455|doi=10.1016/S0169-5347(03)00189-7|issn=0169-5347|hdl=1834/546|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Roberts CM, McClean CJ, Veron JE, Hawkins JP, Allen GR, McAllister DE, Mittermeier CG, Schueler FW, Spalding M, Wells F, Vynne C, Werner TB | display-authors = 6 | title = Marine biodiversity hotspots and conservation priorities for tropical reefs | journal = Science | volume = 295 | issue = 5558 | pages = 1280–4 | date = February 2002 | pmid = 11847338 | doi = 10.1126/science.1067728 | s2cid = 25927433 | bibcode = 2002Sci...295.1280R }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Roberts CM, Andelman S, Branch G, Bustamante RH, Carlos Castilla J, Dugan J, Halpern BS, Lafferty KD, Leslie H, Lubchenco J, McArdle D | display-authors = 6 |date=2003|title=Ecological Criteria for Evaluating Candidate Sites for Marine Reserves |journal=Ecological Applications|language=en|volume=13|issue=sp1|pages=199–214|doi=10.1890/1051-0761(2003)013[0199:ECFECS]2.0.CO;2|issn=1939-5582|doi-access=}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Roberts CM, Hawkins JP, Gell FR | title = The role of marine reserves in achieving sustainable fisheries | journal = Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological Sciences | volume = 360 | issue = 1453 | pages = 123–32 | date = January 2005 | pmid = 15713592 | pmc = 1636100 | doi = 10.1098/rstb.2004.1578 }}</ref> He began his career studying reefs of the [[Red Sea]] in [[Wildlife of Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia]], and has also worked in the [[Wildlife of Maldives|Maldives]] and on the [[Great Barrier Reef]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=16 November 2019|title=Reef Life by Callum Roberts review – miraculous and threatened|url=http://www.theguardian.com/books/2019/nov/16/reef-life-underwater-memoir-callum-roberts-review|access-date=16 April 2021|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref>

Roberts is also an active supporter of the [[Deep Sea Conservation Coalition]]. He is the Chief Scientific Advisor to [[Blue Marine Foundation]]<ref name=":0" /> and an Ambassador for [[World Wide Fund for Nature]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Professor Callum Roberts|url=https://www.wwf.org.uk/council-of-ambassadors/professor-callum-roberts|access-date=1 April 2021|website=WWF|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Since 2011 Roberts has written occasional opinion editorials for ''[[The Guardian]]''<ref>{{Cite web|title = Callum Roberts|url = https://www.theguardian.com/profile/callum-roberts|website = The Guardian|access-date = 22 January 2016}}</ref> on various marine conservation topics, including [[overfishing]].<ref>{{Cite news | vauthors = Roberts C |title = We knew fish catches were too high. But it's much worse than we thought|url = https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2016/jan/21/fish-stocks-low-worse-official-figures|newspaper = The Guardian|date = 21 January 2016|access-date = 22 January 2016|issn = 0261-3077|language = en-GB}}</ref> He has also appeared in the documentary films [[The End of the Line (2009 film)|''The End of the Line'']] (2009) and ''[[Seaspiracy]]'' (2021)<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = McVeigh K |date=31 March 2021|title=Seaspiracy: Netflix documentary accused of misrepresentation by participants|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/mar/31/seaspiracy-netflix-documentary-accused-of-misrepresentation-by-participants|access-date=1 April 2021|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> and was chief scientific adviser to the BBC's 2017 documentary series ''[[Blue Planet II]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

He is the author of two award-winning books, ''[[The Unnatural History of the Sea]]'' ([[Rachel Carson Award]], 2007), which examined the impact of human activity and fishing on marine ecosystems over the last thousand years,<ref>{{Cite book | vauthors = Roberts C |title=The Unnatural History of the Sea|date=9 July 2015 |url=https://islandpress.org/books/unnatural-history-sea|access-date=1 April 2021| publisher = Island Press|language=en | isbn = 978-1-59726-102-9 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title='&#39;There were walls of fish, so many you could hardly see the corals|url=https://thebiologist.rsb.org.uk/biologist-features/2019-05-23-14-15-55|access-date=3 April 2021|website=RSB|language=en-gb |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211201040100/https://www.rsb.org.uk//biologist-features/2019-05-23-14-15-55 |archive-date=1 December 2021}}</ref> and ''Ocean of Life'' (Mountbatten Award, 2013), which covers more recent changes in the ocean and proposes reforms to facilitate their recovery.<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Radford T |date=18 November 2013|title=Ocean of Life: How our Seas are Changing, by Callum Roberts – review|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/nov/18/ocean-of-life-how-our-seas-are-changing-review|access-date=1 April 2021|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=7 June 2012|title=Callum Roberts' Ocean of Life is a manifesto for marine management {{!}} Leo Hickman|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/blog/2012/jun/07/callum-roberts-ocean-of-life|access-date=1 April 2021|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> His latest book is ''Reef Life: An Underwater Memoir'' (2019).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

==Other work==

1999-2003. Member of editorial board of Conservation Biology, published by the Society for Conservation Biology.

1997-2000. Member of Editorial board of journal Animal Conservation, published by Cambridge University Press.

1996. Senior editor of the proceedings of a symposium: "Marine reserves: Function and Design" held at the 8th International Coral Reef Symposium, Panama.

1991-1996. Co-editor of Reef Encounter, Newsletter of the International Society for Reef Studies.
